objectives: Write an Apex REST callout whose endpoint uses the callout:NamedCredential/path form so Salesforce supplies authentication.
Explain that named credentials can skip remote site settings for that host and keep secrets out of Apex.
Mock the callout in a test with HttpCalloutMock; never send production tokens.
Place the callout on a request/response path only when INT-001/INT-003 say the caller should wait.
diagnostic_question: You must GET a JSON resource from a sandbox-safe HTTP API in Apex. Where does the URL live, what does req.setEndpoint look like, and how do you test without a live token?
definition: A named credential specifies the callout endpoint URL and authentication parameters in one definition. In Apex, set the HTTP endpoint to a named credential URL: scheme callout:, credential name, optional path and query. Salesforce manages authentication so the class does not store tokens. Remote site settings can be skipped for that named host. ([Named Credentials as Callout Endpoints](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_callouts_named_credentials.htm); [Use the Named Credential in a Callout](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/named-credentials/guide/nc-use-oauth-cred-in-callout.html))
why_it_matters: Hard-coded URLs and Bearer headers fail security review and break when the host changes. Interviewers want callout: plus a test mock, not a live password in the class.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a prepaid courier envelope with the destination already printed. The named credential is the printed envelope (URL plus how postage is paid). Apex only writes the letter (method, body, extra headers) and drops it in the callout: slot. Tests use a fake sorting office (HttpCalloutMock) so you never spend a real badge.
deeper_explanation: Apex pattern: HttpRequest setEndpoint('callout:My_Named_Credential/some_path'), setMethod('GET' or 'POST'), Http.send. Optional query string after ?. Salesforce generates a standard authorization header unless disabled. Merge fields can build headers/bodies—use the current merge-field table, do not invent names. ([Apex named credential callouts](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_callouts_named_credentials.htm))
Preferred credential model (INT-004): named credential = URL + HTTP; external credential = protocol + principals; encrypted tokens. This procedure assumes that pair already exists in the sandbox.

Callouts are request/response HTTP. They belong on INT-003 request/response paths. After DML in the same transaction, uncommitted work can block callouts—Needs verification of the current 'uncommitted work pending' rule in the Apex callouts guide before quoting edge cases. Async (@future/Queueable) is a common split; job choice is APEX-011.

Tests: implement HttpCalloutMock, Test.setMock, assert status and parsed JSON. Never assert on production secrets. Timeout defaults are versioned—Needs verification; setTimeout explicitly in labs when the guide shows it.

mental_model.analogy: A prepaid courier envelope: named credential prints the address and postage; Apex writes the letter; HttpCalloutMock is a fake sorting office for tests.
useful_mapping: callout:Name/path → drop slot on the envelope
generated Authorization header → postage stamp applied at the counter
raw https URL + Bearer in Apex → writing the account number on the letter
where_it_breaks: Envelope does not choose Bulk vs REST (INT-002).
Mocked tests do not prove the remote OAuth dance.
Merge fields and header-generation flags are real and documented—do not guess them.
Callout limits/timeouts are governors—cite current Apex guide, do not invent numbers.

claims.claim: Named credential URLs use scheme callout:, the credential name, and an optional path. Example form: callout:My_Named_Credential/some_path. Query strings use ?.
Salesforce manages authentication for Apex callouts that specify a named credential, so code does not have to. Remote site settings can be skipped for the named credential's site.
claims.validation: Apex guide plus Use the Named Credential in a Callout.

claims.claim: Salesforce can generate a standard authorization header for named-credential callouts; the option can be disabled. Header/body merge fields are documented on the child topic.
A named credential specifies endpoint URL and HTTP transport; an external credential authenticates. Apex callouts are a supported callout type for named credentials.

changed_in_release: Use Winter '23+ named/external credentials. Reverify merge fields and callout-after-DML rules for API 67.0.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: I never put the URL or Bearer in Apex. Endpoint is callout:NamedCredential/path. Salesforce applies auth from the external credential. Tests use HttpCalloutMock.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: INT-004 already created the named and external credentials. This procedure is HttpRequest, setMethod, send, parse JSON, branch on HTTP status from INT-005. If the user must not wait, I wrap in async (APEX-011). I skip remote site settings because the named credential defines the host. I will not invent timeout numbers.

when_to_use: When implementing a REST callout using a named credential from Apex after INT-004 credentials exist.
When replacing hardcoded URLs or Bearer tokens in Apex with callout:NamedCredential/path.
When tests must mock HTTP instead of using real OAuth tokens.
When the integration style is request/response (INT-003) and a named credential should carry auth.
When you want Salesforce to skip remote site settings for that named host.
when_not_to_use: Do not use an Apex REST callout for a 50,000-row nightly load that belongs on Bulk API 2.0 (INT-002).
Do not put named-credential secrets in the Apex class as a shortcut.
Do not call production endpoints from this lab, or skip HttpCalloutMock in tests.
Do not invent merge-field names or timeout numbers.
Do not treat this procedure as inbound connected-app OAuth (INT-004).

interview_questions.question: How do you implement a REST callout using a named credential?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: HttpRequest endpoint callout:Name/path, set method, send, read status. Tokens stay on the external credential. Tests mock HTTP.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I assume INT-004 already built named plus external credentials. Apex has no Bearer. I skip remote site for that host. I parse JSON and branch on 200/201/4xx. If the UI must not wait, Queueable. I will not invent merge fields.
interview_questions.example: LAB_HttpBinClient GET /get in a sandbox with a mock test.

interview_questions.question: Why named credentials instead of a URL constant?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: URL and auth stay in one managed definition; Apex keeps working if the host changes; secrets are not in source; remote site can be skipped.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: The Apex guide says Salesforce manages authentication and that updating the named credential updates all callouts. That is maintenance and token safety together.
interview_questions.example: Endpoint moves from vendor-test to vendor-stage by editing the credential, not the class.

interview_questions.question: Trigger must notify a REST API on Opportunity close. Sketch the Apex.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: If user must wait, this callout is request/response. If not, Queueable using the same callout: endpoint. Never loop 5,000 send()s from Data Loader.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I check uncommitted work: insert then callout may need async after commit. I mock in tests. I log status not tokens. Style decision is INT-003; this topic is the envelope.
interview_questions.example: Closed Won LAB_Opportunity in sandbox, mock 201.

interview_questions.question: Test suite fails in CI without internet. What did you miss?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: HttpCalloutMock / Test.setMock. Named credentials do not replace mocks.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: CI should never hold production refresh tokens. I assert getEndpoint starts with callout: in a unit test that does not send. Optional live test is a separate manual sandbox check.
interview_questions.example: GitHub Actions running Apex tests for LAB_HttpBinClient.

interview_questions.question: Callout error unauthorized endpoint.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Usually a raw URL without remote site, or a misspelled named credential developer name.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I print req.getEndpoint() in a sandbox debug without secrets. I confirm callout:Name matches Setup. I do not invent OAuth grant bodies. INT-004 if the name is right but 401 comes back from the vendor.
interview_questions.example: Typo callout:LAB_HttpBinn/get instead of callout:LAB_HttpBin/get in sandbox Apex.

interview_questions.question: Works in execute anonymous, fails in trigger with uncommitted work.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: DML before callout in the same transaction. Split with async after commit or callout first per current guide.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I will not claim a named credential bug. I draw the transaction. Queueable is a typical fix; job types are APEX-011. Tests must mock both paths.
interview_questions.example: Before-insert trigger that inserts a log then callouts.

interview_questions.question: Disable generated authorization header—when?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Only when the documented merge-field/header approach requires a custom scheme. Default is generate the header.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I will not disable it to paste a token. I open the custom headers child topic rather than inventing merge names. Per-user vs named principal still comes from INT-004.
interview_questions.example: Vendor wants a non-Bearer custom header documented in their API and in Salesforce merge fields.

interview_questions.question: Teach the prepaid-envelope analogy and where it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Named credential prints address and postage; Apex writes the letter; mock is a fake sorting office. It breaks for Bulk trains and for invented timeouts.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I show callout:LAB_HttpBin/get on the envelope. Live OAuth is not proven by the mock. Apex governors are not postage rates I invent, and a named credential still needs HttpCalloutMock in tests.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard the LAB_HttpBinClient plus test mock.
